items.title: Ron Carter — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Eric Dolphy played saxophone and flute, Dennis Budimir, guitar player, Nathan Gershman, cello player and Chico and me.

ctx.x: I didn't know those guys so I was kinda by myself. But it was okay. I'd had … I didn't socialize much with anybody other than the band to find out what the library was like and how

the arrangements …I was more into the group. Eric Dolphy played saxophone and flute, Dennis Budimir, guitar player, Nathan Gershman, cello player and Chico and me. I wanted to learn how the library was working, how the songs were put together, what's the form of this tune. So my chance to be a part of the bigger picture … it was limited to being a part of this quintet. Those guys couldn't tell me how to play the bass book. And they didn't know Chico's music, so they couldn't really help me along those lines. I…
What was it like for a country boy to tour on a bus in those years, in those places?

items.title: Ron Carter interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 17, 1999
items.q: Eric and I — Eric Dolphy and I stayed in New York, and Chico disbanded, and Chico and the band went to California.

ctx.x: He decided to go west and you stayed?

Eric and I — Eric Dolphy and I stayed in New York, and Chico disbanded, and Chico and the band went to California. The guitar player now is one of the oldest studio guys and the cello player is probably retired, he’s probably close to 85 by now, so the band disbanded.

When you were with Miles, I was just looking at some dates today, and I guess I didn’t quite realize that you were, everyone in that band was a young man, you were 26 or something like that, and of course Tony Williams was younger and Herbie was about—
